newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SIXERS, NETS COMPLETE EIGHT-PLAYER SWAP.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SIXERS, NETS COMPLETE EIGHT-PLAYER SWAP.

text.p: The Philadelphia 76ers and New Jersey Nets on Friday announced completion of their eight-player deal which was worked out on draft day but delayed by objections of the Boston Celtics.

The 76ers sent forward Keith Van Horn, the second overall selection in Wednesday's NBA Draft, guard Lucious Harris, forward Don MacLean and centre Michael Cage to the Nets for guard Jim Jackson, centre Eric Montross and two first-round draft picks -- forward Tim Thomas, the seventh overall pick, and guard Anthony Parker, the 21st overall selection.

The trade was delayed more than 24 hours due to a grievance filed by the Celtics because Cage had been part of last Friday's deal between the Sixers and Celtics that sent forward Dino Radja to Philadelphia.

Radja at first balked at reporting and then failed a physical administered by 76ers doctors on Tuesday that nullified the deal. The Celtics claimed Radja was healthy enough to pass the physical and asked the NBA to settle the matter.
The NBA was to hold a hearing on the dispute Friday morning, but the Celtics rescinded their appeal late Thursday, clearing the way for the deal between Nets and 76ers.
The Nets wanted the highly-regarded Van Horn badly enough to trade away two first-round picks and inherit two other players with multi-year contracts -- Harris and MacLean.
The 6-10 (2.08 m) Van Horn averaged 22 points and 9.5 rebounds per game for Utah last season and was named Western Athletic Conference Player of the Year for the third year running.
Harris averaged 5.4 points in the the first year of a seven-year contract and MacLean averaged 10.9 points as he began a five-year pact with the 76ers.

The Nets had acquired Jackson and Montross in a record nine-player deal with the Dallas Mavericks in February. Jackson averaged 15.9 points and 4.1 assists per game and Montross average 4.4 points and 6.6 rebounds last season.
Jackson's contract expires after the 1997-98 season. Montross can exercise an option in his deal to become a free agent July 1, but has said that he will not.
The 35-year-old Cage has played for the Los Angeles Clippers, Seattle, Cleveland and Philadelphia in his 13-year career and was very nearly a Boston Celtic.
The durable Cage appeared in all 82 games in 1996-97, averaging 1.8 points and 3.9 rebounds, and has played in 657 consecutive games -- the second-longest active streak in the NBA.

The 6-9 (2.05 m) Thomas played just one year at Villanova and averaged 16.9 points and six rebounds before announcing his intentions to turn pro. He was the Big East Conference Rookie of the Year and is expected to play small forward for Philadelphia.

Parker had a solid senior season at Bradley after missing the first nine games with a broken foot, averaging 16.6 points per game. His best season came as a junior, when he averaged 18.9 points on 47.2 percent shooting from the field, including 42.2 percent from three-point range.
